# Always-on Usage
> A usage and workflow encyclopedia for always-on agents (Grok Bot, OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse): which one fits which job, what burns quota, and how to set them up cheaply. For people who want to run bots long-term without burning their quota. An evaluation layer, not a template directory. Comparisons and the calculator are directional estimates, not vendor SLAs; cases aggregate public posts (1838 items plus 26 X stories), each with its author and original link. Grok Bot has the most entries; public Dots and Muse cases are added round by round. Published by Incidental AI.

- Site: https://usage.incidental.site/
- Languages: en (default), zh-CN, zh-TW, ja, ko, ms, vi, fr, es, de — append ?lang=<code>
- Sitemap: https://usage.incidental.site/sitemap.xml
- Full text for LLMs: https://usage.incidental.site/llms-full.txt
- Last updated: 2026-10-23T12:39:47.308Z

## Agents (directional estimates)
### Grok Bot (xAI)
- Good for: Multi-Bot teamwork, email/calendar triage, browser research and form prep
- Quota risk: Medium–high
- Triggers: Scheduled routines, email/webhook, chat, Bot-to-Bot messages
- Browser or connector: Built-in cloud browser + many connectors (Gmail, Calendar, Notion, GitHub…); browser steps cost the most
- Parallelism: Many Bots in parallel, can spawn sub-agents; parallel count is the main quota multiplier
- Routine frequency: Minutes to daily; frequent polling burns quota fastest
- Good for: Multi-Bot teamwork, email/calendar triage, browser research and form prep
- Not good for: Second-level monitoring, scraping farms, unattended high-frequency browser loops

### OpenAI Dots (OpenAI)
- Good for: Daily briefs, follow-up reminders, doc tidying
- Quota risk: Medium
- Triggers: Scheduled tasks, chat, some app events (estimate)
- Browser or connector: Mostly connectors / tool calls; browsing agent on demand
- Parallelism: Mainly one agent, many tasks; limited parallelism (estimate)
- Routine frequency: Daily / weekly digests are most common
- Good for: Daily briefs, follow-up reminders, doc tidying
- Not good for: Long workflows that need several agents

### Meta Muse (Meta)
- Good for: Social content scheduling, light assistant inside messaging apps
- Quota risk: Low–medium
- Triggers: Chat, social/message events, scheduled reminders (estimate)
- Browser or connector: Leans on own-ecosystem connectors; weaker general browsing (estimate)
- Parallelism: Mostly single agent (estimate)
- Routine frequency: Daily reminders / content scheduling
- Good for: Social content scheduling, light assistant inside messaging apps
- Not good for: Deep cross-SaaS automation, flows needing real browser logins

## Calculator rules
- Bots: 3 to 5 bots +1 point, 6 or more +2 points
- Browser: on +1 point
- Frequency: daily +1 point, hourly +2 points
- Result: 0-1 points low, 2-3 medium, 4 or more high

### Grok Bot 0.58.0: screen view moved under Bot name (staff)

- Summary: Staff (@kevinn, 2026-09-24): in Grok Bot 0.58.0 the separate top-right computer button was folded into the Bot’s name at the top center—open the Bot chat, click the name, Back to details, then the live screen preview at the top of that panel (fixes “screen view disappeared” / fully collapsed divider).

### Print via registered local computer only (no home-LAN printers)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/print-via-registered-local-computer-only-no-home-lan-printer-280.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-native-direct-printer-support-for-agents-skip-registered-mac-lp-bridge/172798
- Summary: Staff (kevinn, 2026-09-23): agents run on a cloud computer and cannot see home-network printers—send the file to any signed-in Grok Bot desktop machine that has the printer, then print there; set Settings → Computer → “Execution on this computer” to Always allow to cut approval friction (Auto-review still checks).

### No per-bot reasoning effort control (staff)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/no-per-bot-reasoning-effort-control-staff-281.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-per-agent-reasoning-effort-control-low-mid-full/172822
- Summary: Staff (kevinn, 2026-09-23): there is no per-agent reasoning-effort control in Bot or chat settings—Grok Bot chooses how much reasoning a turn gets, and you cannot set it per bot, role, or template yet (team aware).

### Route-through-desktop only reaches public IPs (not private / split-horizon)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/route-through-desktop-only-reaches-public-ips-not-private-sp-282.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-route-traffic-through-this-computer-fails-for-split-horizon-internal-dev-hosts/172715
- Summary: Staff (deanrie, 2026-09-23): “Route traffic through this computer” only relays to public internet addresses—desktop rejects CONNECT when the hostname resolves to private ranges (192.168/10/172.16–31); public cloud hosts still work. Docs currently imply internal hosts should work; mismatch filed with the team (no ETA).

### Origin CLI on Grok Bot is read-only; merge via UI or your machine
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/origin-cli-on-grok-bot-is-read-only-merge-via-ui-or-your-mac-283.html

- Summary: Staff (kevinn): Grok Bot’s Origin CLI is intentionally read-only (repos/PRs/diffs/checks); undraft/merge isn’t direct yet—ask cloud agents to open PRs ready-for-review, then merge on cursor.com/codebase or `origin pr merge` locally.

- Summary: Staff: Grok-launched cloud agents do appear on cursor.com/agents — enable the Source → Grok Bot filter; middle-click “Open in Cursor” opens the same agent in the browser.

- Summary: Staff: a days-long “Can’t reach your computer” can be a stuck hosted box that Reset / Recover / reinstall cannot clear; staff restores it on their side, then fully quit and reopen the app.

- Summary: Staff: a fresh-install white window is a local profile bug, not a stuck cloud computer; fully quit, rename ~/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot to Grok Bot.bak, then relaunch — reinstall alone will not clear it.

- Summary: Staff: Grok-spawned Cursor Cloud Agents can start in Fast even when your default is not; hover Cursor Grok 4.6 → Edit and uncheck Fast, and switch the follow-up box back if it flips.

### Does GrokBot not have access to my Cursor Codebase?
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/does-grokbot-not-have-access-to-my-cursor-codebase-339.html

- Summary: Staff: Grok Bot has no codebase plugin and does not index your repo; coding work is handed to a Cursor Cloud Agent on a GitHub-connected account (Dashboard → Integrations), with an optional GitHub PAT connector for read-only, auto-created repos from scratch, and no Origin access yet.

### Phantom in Grok Bot is a Mess
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/phantom-in-grok-bot-is-a-mess-340.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/phantom-in-grok-bot-is-a-mess/169930
- Summary: Staff: the Phantom plugin runs on @phantom/mcp-server and each new auth creates a separate dedicated agent wallet, not your personal Phantom wallet, so reconnects show a new address while funded funds stay on the old agent wallet (recover via chat history or Phantom Support).

### Grokbot custom connectors
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grokbot-custom-connectors-341.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grokbot-custom-connectors/169965
- Summary: Staff: there is no settings form for custom connectors; tell the Bot in chat to add an MCP server (public HTTPS streamable HTTP/SSE), confirm the details, and new tools appear from the next message — localhost-only MCP on your PC is unreachable from the cloud computer.

### Grok Bot: Drive MCP should write Google Docs body and Sheet cells, not only file metadata
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-drive-mcp-should-write-google-docs-body-and-sheet-c-342.html

- Summary: Staff: in-place Google Doc/Sheet editing lives in the dedicated Docs and Sheets connectors (edit content against the existing file ID), while Drive is file-level only; add both from the connector marketplace with the same Google account.

### Blank screen after opening Grok Bot
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/blank-screen-after-opening-grok-bot-343.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/blank-screen-after-opening-grok-bot/169966
- Summary: Staff: a blank/white screen usually means the desktop app cannot reach the cloud computer; Cloudflare WARP can intercept that traffic even on a hotspot — turn WARP off or use split tunneling/excluded routes, and prefer builds after 0.28.0 that show an error+retry instead of a blank screen.

### Can't reach your computer from last 72 hours

- Summary: Staff: when the cloud computer is healthy but the app still says Can’t reach, set both IPv4 and IPv6 DNS to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 (JioFiber routers often keep IPv6 DNS) or confirm via a phone hotspot on another carrier.

### Grok Bot Zoom plugin OAuth hardcodes http://localhost:8787/callback — Zoom rejects hostname localhost (error 4700)

- Summary: Staff: the catalog Zoom plugin OAuth hardcodes http://localhost:8787/callback, which Zoom rejects (error 4700); no user workaround until the redirect moves off localhost (e.g. 127.0.0.1).

### Grok Bot Computer Stuck in Partial State — Reset Failed, Existing Cloud Computer Unreachable

### Grok Bot 0.30.0 (Windows) — setup fails with Can't reach your computer, all network checks pass

- Summary: Staff: the app reaches a per-computer subdomain under cursorvm.com, not the apex — if nslookup test123.us8.cursorvm.com is Query refused while the apex works, change DNS on both IPv4 and IPv6 (router RA can keep the ISP resolver even after 1.1.1.1).

### Cloud computer wipes packages after rebuild
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/cloud-computer-wipes-packages-after-rebuild-352.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/cloud-computer-wipes-packages-after-rebuild/169847
- Summary: Staff: Update Computer keeps files and logins but rebuilds the OS image, so apt/apps/daemons are gone; the box also sleeps when idle (background processes die) and can auto-update during idle — keep a package list in a file and ask the Bot to reinstall after an update.

- Summary: Staff: /review and /review-bugbot do not attach to cloud agents created by Grok Bot (decided at create time); start a new agent from cursor.com/agents on the same PR branch and include /review-bugbot there.

- Summary: Staff: “Always allow” for local-computer actions lives only in the desktop app on that machine; iOS can only one-time-approve, and those approvals clear on every new message—set Always Allow under desktop Settings → Execution on Local Computer.

### Wrangler/box auth reminder stays stuck after auth already succeeded via another path

- Summary: Staff: the “help on its computer” / Waiting-for-you reminder only clears when you answer that card (“I’m done, continue” or Skip) or send any chat message—it does not auto-dismiss if the Bot finished login another way.

### Fastmail Filters & Rules Save is a silent no-op (Chrome on the box)

- Summary: Staff: Fastmail Settings → Filters & Rules Save on the box Chrome fires zero network requests; workaround is manage filters/Sieve via Fastmail’s API (JMAP) with a token—the mail helper already uses that path successfully.

### VPN, SSO, Passkey, and YubiKey Within Grokbot
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/vpn-sso-passkey-and-yubikey-within-grokbot-359.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/vpn-sso-passkey-and-yubikey-within-grokbot/170148
- Summary: Staff: Grok Bot’s cloud computer cannot join a corporate VPN today (don’t install a VPN client on it — that can knock the box offline); Atlassian Cloud / public SSO works via browser takeover (Okta etc.), YubiKey works on macOS/Windows under Settings → Security Key, and internal VPN-only sites need Execution on Local Computer on your VPN’d machine.

### Unable to connect
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/unable-to-connect-360.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/unable-to-connect/170123
- Summary: Staff: chats and agents live on the hosted Grok Bot computer — during an outage recovery that computer can be temporarily replaced with a blank one (roster looks empty); Cursor can restore it from saved data, then quit and reopen the app to see agents/history again.

### GrokBot Linux Execution on Local Computer not working
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grokbot-linux-execution-on-local-computer-not-working-361.html

- Summary: Staff: empty ListMachines / local execution failing on Grok Bot 0.30.0 Linux is a known bug with a fix already merged for the next desktop update; interim workaround is an unlocked system keyring (gnome-keyring or KWallet), fully quit leftover Grok Bot processes, then relaunch.

### New report, Windows, leftover daemon on 0.30.0
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/new-report-windows-leftover-daemon-on-0-30-0-362.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/new-report-windows-leftover-daemon-on-0-30-0/170121
- Summary: Staff: 0.30.0 fixed one macOS daemon exit/no-respawn path, but Windows leftover local-exec-daemon is a different known failure; when the machine is unreachable, Quit from the tray, end remaining “Grok Bot” and local-exec-daemon processes in Task Manager, relaunch, and wait about a minute to re-register.

### Grok bot failed to respond
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-failed-to-respond-363.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-failed-to-respond/170235
- Summary: Staff (kevinn): “Bot failed to respond” on every bot—including fresh copies—means the shared cloud computer is stuck, not something you can fix by restarting or recreating bots; after staff recovery, fully quit (Cmd+Q / force-close iOS), update every install, keep one open, and test in a new chat.

### Grok Bot 0.30.0 Stuck on Black Loading Screen During Initial Setup on Mac
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-0-30-0-stuck-on-black-loading-screen-during-initial-364.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-0-30-0-stuck-on-black-loading-screen-during-initial-setup-on-mac/170251
- Summary: Staff (Colin): Team admin role alone does not provision a Grok Bot computer — Grok Bot is included with a paid team seat (Standard or Premium), not the admin role. If the signed-in account has no seat, the app sits on the black loading screen with no computer to reset. Fix: assign yourself a seat in Cursor dashboard Members, fully quit and reopen Grok Bot; or sign in with a seated team account.

### Grok Bot Windows — fresh profile setup fails with “Can’t reach your computer” after backend fix
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-windows-fresh-profile-setup-fails-with-can-t-reach--365.html

- Summary: Staff (deanrie): Grok Bot ignores the Windows system proxy / local HTTP proxy and connects direct to the Agent Computer — so DNS/TCP/CONNECT checks through a proxy can pass while the app fails. Use VPN/proxy TUN (Enhanced/Global/virtual adapter) mode, then verify with curl.exe --noproxy "*" -I https://test123.<region>.cursorvm.com (expect 404 awselb/2.0). User confirmed TUN fixed setup. ### Grok Bot 0.30.0 stuck on black loading screen on Windows 11
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-0-30-0-stuck-on-black-loading-screen-on-windows-11-366.html

- Summary: Staff (Colin): Healthy cloud computer + black spinner on both LAN and hotspot can be Zscaler Client Connector still tunneling (including on hotspot). Quit Grok Bot, pause/disable Zscaler, relaunch; ask IT to allowlist/exclude SSL inspection for *.cursorvm.com and **.cursorvm.com (both levels).

### Grok Bot 0.30.0 — Agent Computer unreachable after Update, Recover, and Reset all failed
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-0-30-0-agent-computer-unreachable-after-update-reco-367.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-0-30-0-agent-computer-unreachable-after-update-recover-and-reset-all-failed/170258
- Summary: Staff (kevinn): An “Aw, Snap!” Chrome page on the Bot screen after idle wake is the Bot’s browser crashing inside a healthy computer — reload the tab or ask the Bot to reload, fully quit/reopen Grok Bot if needed, and do not run Update/Recover/Reset; idle machines take a moment to wake and a first message can miss, so resend is safe.

### Grok Bot Mac “unavailable” after password reset (expired session)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-mac-unavailable-after-password-reset-expired-sessio-368.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-mac-blocked-after-password-change-app-says-unavailable-spending-shows-supergrok-plus/170389
- Summary: Staff (deanrie): After a password reset, Grok Bot on Mac can keep an expired session and show “isn’t available on this account yet” even though SuperGrok/Cursor access and your cloud computer/Bots are fine — Log out from the bottom of that screen, fully Quit (Cmd+Q), reopen and Sign in with the new password; Check Access→download is a misleading expired-session UI, not a missing entitlement.

### Homepage “Approval needed” stuck after card timeout
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/homepage-approval-needed-stuck-after-card-timeout-369.html

- Summary: Staff (Colin): A homepage “Approval needed” tile with nothing pending usually means an approval card timed out (~10 minutes unanswered); open the agent and send a short message or restart the app to clear a stuck badge — the tile is supposed to clear when the card expires.

### File contents and grokbot — viewer Copy vs Download
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/file-contents-and-grokbot-viewer-copy-vs-download-370.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/file-contents-and-grokbot/170421
- Summary: Staff (Colin): The in-app file viewer only offers Download today; for .md/.txt you can click-drag to select and Cmd/Ctrl+C, while .docx/.pdf won’t highlight — ask the Bot to paste the full text into chat and use the message Copy action as a workaround.

### Grok Bot Canva connector failing — Invalid redirect URI on iOS
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-canva-connector-failing-invalid-redirect-uri-on-ios-371.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-canva-connector-failing/170431
- Summary: Staff (deanrie): Canva “Invalid redirect URI” on Grok Bot iOS 1.4.0 is a known app-link vs web-redirect mismatch (not your Canva settings) — connect Canva from desktop Grok Bot on the same account and the connector syncs to iPhone.

### Local computer looks connected but CopyFromBox/Shell flaps after large transfer timeout
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/local-computer-looks-connected-but-copyfrombox-shell-flaps-a-372.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-local-computer-execution-looks-connected-in-settings-but-is-not-actually-usable-for-file-i-o/169877
- Summary: Staff (deanrie): A large CopyFromBox (or timed-out Shell) can drop the local machine from the agent list for ~1 minute while Settings still says connected — split big copies, wait a minute before retrying, and if stuck Cmd+Q then pkill -f local-exec-daemon and reopen.

### Grok Bot Windows — Can't reach computer on Free plan / after SuperGrok link
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-windows-can-t-reach-computer-on-free-plan-after-sup-373.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-windows-cant-reach-computer/170462
- Summary: Staff (deanrie): “Can't reach computer” can mean the signed-in Cursor account is Free with no Grok Bot entitlement (not DNS)—link SuperGrok on the same Cursor account via cursor.com, then fully sign out/in (or Quit from the Windows tray) so the desktop app refreshes access.

### Grokbot failing to connect to cloud agent — Privacy Mode (Legacy) false positive
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grokbot-failing-to-connect-to-cloud-agent-privacy-mode-legac-374.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grokbot-failing-to-connect-to-cloud-agent/170486
- Summary: Staff (deanrie): Launching a Cloud Agent from Grok Bot can falsely hit the “Privacy Mode (Legacy)” check after a recent release even when your account uses current Privacy Mode—Cursor Desktop launch still works; sign-out/reset won’t help; staff are tracking a server-side fix.

### Grok Bot 0.39.0 first setup: Reconnecting forever until Privacy Mode is saved
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-0-39-0-first-setup-reconnecting-forever-until-priva-375.html
- Type: field-case · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-0-39-0-first-setup-reconnecting-to-your-computer-forever-mac/170509
- Summary: Staff (deanrie): First-setup “Reconnecting to your computer” can mean the account never saved an explicit Privacy Mode choice (data notice alone is not enough)—set Privacy Mode in cursor.com/dashboard → Settings → Privacy, fully Quit (Cmd+Q), reopen; Retry/Recover/Reset will not fix a missing privacy choice.

### Status beat leaks between bots — one Bot memory across 1:1 and groups

### Unreachable from Bot OOM / parallel fan-out
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/unreachable-from-bot-oom-parallel-fan-out-417.html

- Summary: Staff (mohitjain): Recurring unreachable can be Agent Computer OOM when a Bot spins too many parallel processes—not your network. Prevention: worker concurrency 1 on production paths, no mass-resume after rematerialize, batch large fan-outs; avoid Reset while support restores.

### Keep Grok Bot from acting before you have looked
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/x-kv1nsiii-2113231986567315966.html

- Summary: The author warns that with loose rules Grok Bot reacts to new messages and calendar shifts by replying and booking on its own. His rules: read first and draft only for real changes, stop empty checks after one look, surface only items that need your tap, send or book nothing without you, and note small shifts instead of making tasks.

### Grok Bot drops connector calls after two minutes, so cap waits at 100 s
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/gh-github-com-foxkill-steerlink-pull-16.html
- Type: guide · Product: grok-bot · Author: foxkill · Source: https://github.com/foxkill/steerlink/pull/16 · Date: 2026-10-22
- Summary: A test in Grok Bot showed it calls get_session_updates with wait_seconds: 120, while Grok Bot gives up on a connector call after two minutes without progress. Version 0.1.11 caps each wait at 100 s for hosts that do not ask for progress, returning status: running so the next call continues; hosts with a progressToken keep the full wait and get progress every 10 s.

### Letting Grok Bot or a Dot drive local Codex and Claude CLIs
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/gh-github-com-snseam-harnessorbit-pull-14.html
- Type: field-case · Product: multi · Author: Snseam · Source: https://github.com/Snseam/harnessorbit/pull/14 · Date: 2026-10-21
- Summary: Phase one of HarnessOrbit's agent access layer: a remote personal agent such as Grok Bot or a Dot, without a shell, authenticates as a scoped principal, submits a job that runs the local Codex or Claude CLI in an isolated worktree, and polls status until a decision is needed. ### Don't build a bot team on day one: one topic, one bot
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/x-andresruggiero3-2112671200291811680.html

- Summary: The author calls it the most common Grok Bot overcomplication: separate bills, subscriptions, budget and reminder bots for home finances. One money bot can find subscriptions, flag unused ones, remind you before bills are due and send a weekly summary. It keeps all the context, uses fewer tokens and has one set of instructions. Split only when the job is genuinely different.

### A practical setup guide for lead research with Grok Bot
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/x-earifcom-2111032337710637266.html
- Type: guide · Product: grok-bot · Author: earifcom · Source: https://x.com/earifcom/status/2111032337710637266 · Date: 2026-10-16
- Summary: The author proposes an adaptable setup: write a one-page brief (offer, buyer, current signals, allowed sources, exclusions); create one "Prospect Research Desk" bot that must never guess contacts, send messages or modify the CRM; run a small pilot prompt (up to 5 businesses, at most 15 source pages); review, deduplicate and sort into three statuses; after two useful batches save it as a skill and schedule it on weekdays; only then add a controlled CRM handoff and follow-up. The author notes it is a blueprint, not a client case, and nothing was executed.

### Using Dots as a 7-agent swarm to improve a math bound (Lean-verified)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/hn-49971444.html
- Type: field-case · Product: openai-dots · Author: unexcitedneurons · Source: https://unexcitedneurons.substack.com/p/i-used-openai-dots-as-an-agent-swarm · Date: 2026-10-05
- Summary: The author split a Dot and 6 subagents into research, Lean formalization, computational search, adversarial review and coordination roles; in about 3 days they proved C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (previously 19). The Lean proof passed the Palomar registry's checks but isn't peer-reviewed yet. Lessons: agents grind but don't know when to stop, verification is everything, and when the shared workspace was wiped they rebuilt it from messages.

### Claude Duet vs Grok Bot vs Dots vs Muse
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/x-degensing-2113205821840695736.html

- Summary: Based on reports so far: Duet has no separate price and runs on your Claude plan, Grok Bot starts at $30, Dots at $100, and Muse is free to start. Grok Bot runs several named agents while Duet is one thread; Dots can optionally use your laptop; Duet asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes, and its background checks count toward Claude limits.

### How three proactive agents differ
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/x-curiousdevx-2113216255893409964.html

- Summary: The author sums up: Grok Bot is a team of specialized bots sharing one computer that learn by watching, with a cheaper entry; OpenAI Dots is one primary agent deep in ChatGPT and Slack/Teams with 4,000+ app connections; Claude Duet is judgment-first, messages you first, targets back-office work like invoices, payroll and briefs, and asks before sensitive actions. All three run on a cloud computer.

### Ultra weekly Bot pool: each messaged bot burns a turn
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/ultra-weekly-bot-pool-each-messaged-bot-burns-a-turn-9.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-usage-billing/172769
- Summary: Staff (kevinn, 2026-09-23): on Ultra, Grok Bot has its own weekly allowance separate from Cursor; spawning ~60 bots plus group chats burned usage fast because every bot that receives a message runs its own turn—prefer fewer bots (one bot + subagents), delete unused, or enable on-demand under Spending.

### Fleet cost tip: fresh chat per task + quieter Bot-to-Bot handoffs
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/fleet-cost-tip-fresh-chat-per-task-quieter-bot-to-bot-handof-10.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/1-500-in-one-week-running-a-grok-bot-fleet-expected-or-a-bug/172705
- Summary: Staff (kevinn): each turn re-reads the bot’s full chat history—so week-long threads burn 80–90k tokens/step; use + fresh chat per task, keep Profile/Notion state, silence ack pings between bots, and space Routines (hourly+) to cut fleet spend.

### Grok Bot file handoff limits + QuickTime still+ALAC recipe
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-file-handoff-limits-quicktime-still-alac-recipe-12.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-multi-gb-review-video-undeliverable-still-aac-goes-silent-in-quicktime/172600
- Summary: Staff: chat video cap is 200 MB; Mac CopyFromBox only for small files; connectors cannot take large binaries yet — use H.264 still + ALAC in .mov under the limit for QuickTime.

### Local-exec file tools stay in the user profile root (staff)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/local-exec-file-tools-stay-in-the-user-profile-root-staff-14.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/copyfrombox-and-read-refuse-paths-outside-user-profile-after-0-57-1-outside-the-allowed-local-exec-root/172349
- Summary: Staff (deanrie, 2026-09-19): On a registered machine, Read / CopyFromBox / CopyToBox are limited to the user profile folder (e.g. C:\Users\<you>), while Shell is not—so D:\/G:\ and junctions that resolve outside the profile are rejected by the file tools. Workaround: CopyFromBox into the home folder then move with Shell, or read/copy other drives via Shell (Get-Content / Copy-Item). Team is decidi

- Summary: Staff: agents Grok Bot starts run in your Cursor account and burn Cursor plan usage; Grok Bot chat has a separate allowance; unnamed-model agents use your Cloud Agent default.

- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/weekly-grok-bot-usage-can-spill-into-paid-on-demand-with-no--17.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-gives-no-warning-before-weekly-usage-spills-into-paid-on-demand/169679
- Summary: Staff: spend order is Grok Bot weekly allowance, then referral/promo credits, then paid On-Demand, with no in-app warning; a $0 On-Demand cap does not block credits, so pause near 100% weekly meter if you want no spill.

### Pro weekly pool is separate; overflow hits shared On-Demand
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/pro-weekly-pool-is-separate-overflow-hits-shared-on-demand-18.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-spend-cursor-usage-i-cant-accept-it/169796
- Summary: Staff correction: on Pro, Grok Bot has its own included weekly pool, separate from Cursor plan usage; overflow still bills the shared On-Demand pool, so set a $0 On-Demand cap if you want no paid spill.

### Access is live for paid plans, not legacy request-based
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/access-is-live-for-paid-plans-not-legacy-request-based-19.html

- Summary: Staff: Grok Bot is live for all paid individual plans (Pro / Pro+ / Ultra) and self-serve Teams with no percent or region rollout; legacy request-based pricing does not get it unless you opt into usage-based.

### Local CLI orchestration and always-allow are intended use
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/local-cli-orchestration-and-always-allow-are-intended-use-20.html

- Summary: Staff: local-CLI orchestration (including Cursor CLI), always-allow local execution, and authenticated browser sessions are intended Grok Bot use; third-party ToS stay separate, bots share one computer, and a continuous Pro orchestrator burns the weekly pool fast.

### Grok Bot does not spend Pro $20 IDE credit
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-does-not-spend-pro-20-ide-credit-21.html

- Summary: Staff: Pro’s $20 Other Models credit is not Grok Bot’s weekly pool; dashboard “Included in Pro” is shared billing — and with On-Demand off the Bot can still drain Cursor credits (referral/promo) before stopping (see 169982).

### Grok Bot draining Cursor credit pool
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-draining-cursor-credit-pool-22.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-draining-cursor-credit-pool/169982
- Summary: Staff: after the Grok Bot weekly pool on Pro+ is gone, usage keeps going onto Cursor credits (referral/promo) first, then on-demand if enabled; a $0 on-demand cap stops paid overage but not credit drain, and claude-opus / grok-4.6-high-fast lines are models the Bot picks server-side.

### Grok Bot: weekly usage hits 100% after bot-to-bot reviews the user asked to stop
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-weekly-usage-hits-100-after-bot-to-bot-reviews-the--23.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-weekly-usage-hits-100-after-bot-to-bot-reviews-the-user-asked-to-stop/170271
- Summary: Staff (mohitjain): Each bot-to-bot message burns a weekly-usage turn; asking bots in chat to “stay quiet” is only a hint. Reliable fixes: run work in one Command Agent with subagents (they finish and stop), and delete unused specialist bots (idle bots can still be woken; deleting also clears that bot’s chat — save first). Double limit banners are blocked retries, not double charges.

### Grok Bot cannot attach inline images to Cursor bug reports (chat drop and forum upload)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-cannot-attach-inline-images-to-cursor-bug-reports-c-24.html

- Summary: Staff (mohitjain): To get a screenshot into Grok Bot chat, use the composer + button (or drag a saved file) and wait for the thumbnail before send — drag-from-browser/other-app or Enter-before-thumbnail usually drops it. Forum upload by the assistant is a current limitation; attach the screenshot yourself or reply to support email.

### Grok Bot routines don't auto-run on schedule
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/grok-bot-routines-don-t-auto-run-on-schedule-25.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: grok-bot · Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/grok-bot-routines-dont-auto-run-on-schedule/170358
- Summary: Staff (Colin): Editing bot instructions or which platform created a routine does not break schedules — late “Next run: Run now” usually means the slot fired but sat in a queue (often 10–37 min), and some runs finish without posting to chat; don’t recreate routines; message the bot for an on-demand check-in.

### Why does Grok Bot chat use so many sand-* tokens?
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/why-does-grok-bot-chat-use-so-many-sand-tokens-26.html

- Summary: Staff (mohitjain): Conversations use the Grok Bot weekly pool, but routines/automations and browser/CUA actions run as cloud agents on your Cursor plan and can drain Other Models (blocking Claude/GPT) even when the Grok Bot bar still has room—pause heavy grok-bot-automation / grok-bot-cua routines or enable on-demand.

### Shell Auto-review: npm/pnpm/yarn substring blocks before approval card

- Summary: Staff (Colin, 2026-09-07): “executable content could not be bound” can fire in a pre-check before any approval card when the command text contains npm/pnpm/yarn anywhere—including a full path like /workspace/.../bin/npm; until fixed, run PATH=/path/to/node/bin:$PATH npm ci (or npm install / npm run) as a single command with working_directory set—avoid absolute .../npm, npm -v alone, and && chains 

### Weekly allowance lasts longer: fresh chats, space routines, cloud-agent manager

Ultra also includes Cursor IDE/Agent/Cloud Agents; Heavy adds grok.com/Grok app features but not a Cursor plan. The free Cursor Ultra-with-Heavy promo ended end of August. ### Watch out: how a malicious page can hijack Muse via prompt injection
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/medium-watchout-meta-muse-prompt-injection.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: meta-muse · Author: Aizaai Net (HexTyx) · Source: https://medium.com/@aizaai.net/watchout-meta-muse-prompt-injection-how-a-malicious-web-page-can-hijack-an-ai-agent-b3ff1f5f0151 · Date: 2026-10-09
- Summary: Using Meta Muse as a case study, the article explains indirect prompt injection: instructions for the agent hidden in web pages, emails, PDFs or tool output look ordinary to a human but may be acted on by the AI, and with access to private data, browsers, APIs and credentials, that content becomes an attack surface. The author writes for security firm HexTyx.

### Warning: Muse's first weeks of privacy and security problems (Techdirt)
- URL: https://usage.incidental.site/cases/hn-49977588.html
- Type: quota-report · Product: meta-muse · Author: Karl Bode · Source: https://www.techdirt.com/2026/10/06/metas-muse-is-an-adorable-privacy-and-security-dumpster-fire/ · Date: 2026-10-06
- Summary: Techdirt rounds up reports: a zero-day at launch that allowed spying on Mac users; a user whose Marketplace sales Muse handled sold items cheaply and gave out his address (he says he misunderstood the permissions); reports of reading private messages without approval and profiling contacts. Tighten permissions before connecting email, calendar or payments.
